newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.Africa stocks end down, bank shares feature.
newsitem.headline: S.Africa stocks end down, bank shares feature.

text.p: South African shares dipped on Thursday as poo sentiment gripped the market, but sparkling results from Investec Bank Ltd triggered a surge of trade in the banking sector, dealers said.
The local market has been suffering the blues recently after a rash of poor corporate earnings in May crystalised concerns in the industrials sector.
The market also took a knock on Thursday from a dip on Wall Street on Wednesday and failed to respond to an early rise in New York shares on Thursday.

The all-share index dropped 31.1 points to 7,096.1 as the industrials index slipped 44.7 points to 8,351.5. Volumes were modest at 717 million rands worth of trade, but the figure was the highest of the week so far.
The main reason for the higher volumes was the interest sparked in the banking sector following the publication of Investec's year figures after the market closed on Wednesday.

Investec jumped 6.00 rand to end at a new year high of 156.00 rand. Elsewhere in the sector, Absa put on 15 cents to 30.00 rand in trade worth 66.1 million rand, Nedcor droped 25 cents to 89.75 rand in trade worth 47.1 million rand and Standard Bank was steady at 214.00 rand in deals worth 41.0 million rand.

Gold shares had a weaker session after two days of gains as demand slackened and fresh concerns were raised about the price of bullion. Gold fixed a shade easier in London at $342.75 afer New York gold opened lower.
The golds index lost 8.6 points to 1,205.5.
